title: CSV to JSON command-line tool with schema validation
summary: A command-line tool that converts a CSV file to a JSON array using a small schema that gives each column a type and rules, reporting every problem clearly.
users: Analysts and scripts that need clean typed JSON from spreadsheet exports.
interface:
Python 3.11+, standard library only (no pip packages). Package `csv2json/` with `__main__.py`, run as:

```bash
python3 -m csv2json INPUT.csv --schema SCHEMA.json [-o OUTPUT.json]
```

Without `-o`, the JSON goes to standard output. Output is a JSON array of objects, one per data row, keys in schema order, written with `json.dumps(rows, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)`.

Schema file: `{ "columns": { "<name>": { "type": "string"|"integer"|"number"|"boolean", "required"?: bool, "min"?: number, "max"?: number, "pattern"?: regex } } }`.

- The CSV's first row is the header. Its column names must equal the schema's columns as a set.
- Cells are trimmed of surrounding spaces.
- An empty cell becomes `null`, or an error if the column is required.
- `integer` accepts an optional sign and digits only. `number` accepts anything `float()` accepts except nan and inf.
- `boolean` accepts true/false/yes/no/1/0 in any letter case.
- `min` and `max` apply to integer and number. `pattern` is a full match (`re.fullmatch`) on string columns.

Exit codes and messages:

- **0:** success.
- **2:** data errors. Every error is printed to standard error, one per line, as `line <N>: <column>: <message>`, where N is the 1-based physical line number in the file of the row's first line. All rows are checked; no output file is written.
- **1:** usage problems, printed to standard error as one line starting `error: `. These are a missing input or schema file, an invalid schema JSON, unknown type names, and header problems (`error: missing column <name>`, `error: unknown column <name>`).

Input is UTF-8 and may start with a byte-order mark. Quoted fields may contain commas, quotes and newlines (standard CSV).

stories.title: Convert a clean file
stories.iWant: to turn a CSV export into typed JSON
stories.gherkin:
Scenario: typed output
  Given people.csv with columns name, age, active and a matching schema
  When I run python3 -m csv2json people.csv --schema schema.json
  Then exit code is 0
  And stdout is a JSON array where age is a number and active is true or false

stories.title: See every problem at once
stories.iWant: all errors listed with line and column
stories.soThat: I can fix the file in one pass
stories.gherkin:
Scenario: two bad rows
  Given a CSV where line 3 has age "abc" and line 5 has an empty required name
  When I run the tool
  Then exit code is 2
  And stderr has a line starting "line 3: age:" and a line starting "line 5: name:"
  And no output file is written

stories.title: Clear usage errors
stories.gherkin:
Scenario: header mismatch
  Given a CSV header with a column not in the schema
  When I run the tool
  Then exit code is 1
  And stderr is "error: unknown column <name>"

frs.title: Typed conversion
frs.text: When the input and schema are valid, the system shall write a JSON array of objects with values converted per column type, keys in schema order, empty optional cells as null, and exit 0.

frs.title: Type rules
frs.text: The system shall convert integer (optional sign and digits), number (float() without nan or inf), boolean (true/false/yes/no/1/0 in any case) and string, and apply min, max and full-match pattern rules.

frs.title: Report all data errors
frs.text: When any cell breaks a rule, the system shall print one line per error to stderr as line <N>: <column>: <message> with N the physical line of the row's start, check every row, write no output, and exit 2.

frs.title: Usage errors
frs.text: When the input or schema file is missing, the schema is invalid or names an unknown type, or the header does not match the schema columns, the system shall print one line starting "error: " to stderr and exit 1.

frs.title: CSV edge cases
frs.text: The system shall accept a UTF-8 byte-order mark, quoted fields containing commas, quotes and newlines, and surrounding spaces in cells.

nfrs.title: Standard library only
nfrs.text: The tool shall use only the Python standard library.
